title: Thermal Physics and Ideal Gases
seo_title: Year 13 A Level Physics: Thermal Physics and Ideal Gases Worksheets
standard_text: Thermal energy transfer (specific heat capacity and specific latent heat), the ideal gas laws, the equation pV = nRT = NkT, the kinetic theory model and the mean kinetic energy of molecules.
meta_desc: Free Year 13 A level physics worksheets on thermal physics: specific heat capacity, latent heat, gas laws, pV = nRT, molecular kinetic energy and r.m.s. speed. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: pV = nRT = NkT, with T in kelvin.
body_html:
How to think about it

Heating: Q = mcΔθ; changing state: Q = mL. For an ideal gas pV = nRT = NkT, always with T in kelvin (°C + 273).

Boyle's law (constant T): pV constant. Charles's law (constant p): V/T constant. The mean kinetic energy of a molecule is (3/2)kT.

Example

2.0 dm³ at 27 °C heated to 127 °C at constant pressure. New volume?

V/T constant

2.0 × 400/300

Answer: 2.67 dm³

Example

Mean kinetic energy at 300 K?

1.5 × 1.38 × 10−23 × 300

Answer: 6.21 × 10−21 J

Common mistakes

  • Using °C in the gas laws.
  • Using c instead of L when the state changes.
  • Mixing up R (per mole) and k (per molecule).

faq.q: Why must temperatures be in kelvin?
faq.a: The gas laws are proportionalities that start from absolute zero, 0 K = −273 °C.
The energy needed to change the state of 1 kg of a substance without changing its temperature.
